te: Draft report on a quick-win green area policy, and the matter of Siamese rosewood exports
se: The meeting noted progress on the draft study report on a flexible, quick-win policy framework for national forestry and more green area for the country. It links to the 20-year National Strategy and sets green area targets for 2037 in 3 types: natural forest of at least 35 per cent, economic forest of at least 15 per cent, and urban and rural green space of at least 5 per cent of the country's area. Data in the draft report says forest area fell by about 100,000 rai a year on average in 2018–2025. The meeting suggested driving the policy through national committee mechanisms, enforcing the law strictly, and linking GISTDA's forest change alert system with field units. The meeting also noted information on Siamese rosewood exports: the National Forest Policy Committee (22 July 2026) resolved to review a Ministry of Commerce notification so that rosewood from forest plantations could be exported, with the Forest Industry Organization as the sole exporter, and views on this differ. The meeting agreed to propose the matter to the committee and invite the agencies concerned to give information. It also noted a study visit on wild elephants and communities in Nakhon Nayok on 27 November 2026, and extended the wild elephant working group's time by 30 days.
it: Progress on the draft study report: a flexible, quick-win policy framework for national forestry and more green area for the country
Siamese rosewood, log and sawn timber exports and illegal trade: to be proposed to the committee with the agencies concerned invited
Study visit on natural resource management and wild elephants and communities, Nakhon Nayok, 27 November 2026
30-day extension for the working group on an integrated plan for the wild elephant and community crisis

Export duty on mangrove timber from plantations, nursery trees, and planting sappan wood to reduce wild elephant problems
se: The meeting considered 3 matters. First, a request to waive export duty on logs and sawn timber of mangrove trees from plantations with valid title deeds: growers in Samut Songkhram must pay export duty, which makes their prices hard to compete, and mangrove trees take 12–15 years to grow. Bearing in mind the limits of section 32 of the State Fiscal and Financial Discipline Act B.E. 2018, the meeting proposed taking the matter to the National Forest Policy Committee, with the Department of Marine and Coastal Resources gathering the data. Second, nursery-grown trees for transplanting, which help add green areas in cities and are in demand abroad, but still lack traceability and production standards. Third, promoting sappan wood along fences or buffer zones, since trials found that elephants do not eat or damage it, so it can add green areas, earn income and reduce conflict between people and wild elephants.
it: Request to waive export duty on logs and sawn timber of mangrove trees from plantations with valid title deeds
Nursery trees for transplanting and green areas: markets, production standards and traceability
Promoting sappan wood for community enterprises and to reduce the impact of wild elephants

Promoting the use of economic timber and the wood industry
se: The meeting considered ways to promote the use of economic timber to strengthen the grassroots economy and a sustainable wood industry. The Royal Forest Department was invited to give information. It explained licences in the wood industry, the release of restricted timber under section 7 when grown on owned or possessed land, a proposed amendment to the Forest Plantation Act B.E. 1992 expected to be finished around 2028, about 1.4 million rai of registered forest plantations, the online plantation and traceability systems, and planting subsidies. The meeting suggested, for example, that the state help give confidence about markets for slow-growing timber, that seedling handouts focus on target provinces with follow-up on planting, and that land tax relief for green areas be sped up.
it: Promoting the use of economic timber to strengthen the grassroots economy and the wood industry (Royal Forest Department)
Release of restricted timber under section 7, and the proposed amendment to the Forest Plantation Act B.E. 1992
Suggestions: markets for slow-growing timber, seedling handouts with follow-up, and land tax measures for green areas
